steps.text: Design the assignment contract shared by orchestrator, group chat and employee agents: message types for ask (build/step id, required skills/tools/capabilities), claim (first claimer opens the dialog), candidate list with match %, veto window (90 s, deadline timestamp), pick (Brett or default), and brief return (employee brief set to orchestrator). Write it as a versioned contract doc plus JSON schema; reuse the Brownie/Molly handoff envelope instead of a new one.
steps.why: Cross-port contract used by orchestrator, group chat and every employee agent

steps.text: Schema and migration for assignment state: per build/step record with candidates[] {employee, match %, reasons}, claimedBy, vetoDeadline, pickedBy (brett|default), assignedEmployee, and returned brief refs. Extend the orchestrator table's assigned-employee column data instead of adding a parallel store; migrate existing orchestrator.json entries (assignedEmployee stays, new fields empty).
steps.why: Schema + migration design for orchestrator state

steps.text: Match scoring: compute each employee's percentage of being the best choice from their skills, tools and capabilities (employee profiles) against the build/step requirements; normalize to sum 100, ties broken by current load. Pure module with unit-testable inputs.

Orchestrator posts the ask in the group chat when it assigns a build or step (reuse the Brownie/Molly group chat handoff path), records the open assignment, and accepts the first claim; later claims are acknowledged as already taken.

Veto timer: on first claim start the 90 s window (deadline stored, survives restart); Brett's pick ends it early; at expiry the orchestrator assigns the highest-percentage candidate and posts the result in the group chat.

Match dialog UI opened by the claimer: lists all matching agents with percentages and reasons, a live 90 s countdown, pick buttons and a 'keep default' action; show the assigned employee in the orchestrator table column.

API for the dialog and assignment: deep link (console_show / console_open target orchestrator/assign/<build|step id>), state read (candidates, %, deadline, claimedBy, assigned), actions (ask, claim, pick, accept default, cancel) and settings (veto seconds, auto-assign on/off) via console REST routes, MCP console actions/plugin commands, CLI subcommands and AmberX voice intents, all four the same.

Employee brief set: the assigned employee writes the step brief from its own brief templates and its employee data (training data, skills, tools), and sends the brief back to the orchestrator, which attaches it to the build/step and runs the step from it.

API for employee briefs: state read of each employee's brief set and returned briefs, actions to regenerate/resend a brief, through REST, MCP, CLI and voice, with a deep link to the brief in the employee view.

Tests (match scoring, first-claim wins, 90 s default pick, Brett pick, restart mid-window, brief return, API parity REST/MCP/CLI/voice), report at _claude/builds/reports/orchestrator-assigns-builds-steps-to-employee-ag.md, THREADS row, and PR stating how each UI piece is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

after.title: Full API + CLI control of everything, plus an offline index/registry; AI only as fallback
after.detail: 1) Extensive API and CLI control over every page, app, plugin, tool, behavior, display and setting, covering every option and every possible parameter value. Scope: console, Molly, axHub, AmberX app, and through axHub: Hostinger, Coolify, VPS. Moshi is a third-party phone SSH app: cover it only as far as it can be driven (deep links/intents), otherwise record the gap. 2) A complete index and registry of everything controllable (ids, types, actions, parameters, allowed values, where it lives) for offline management and internal logic. 3) Rule: anything that can be done without AI is done without AI. AI is only a fallback, and only when 'Make Claude available to the console' is on in Claude settings. Builds on universal-voice-api-control and the ui-api-parity builds; reuse them, don't duplicate.

split.note: Split by Claude into 17 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Design the control-registry@1 contract: one entry shape for everything controllable (id, type page/app/plugin/tool/behavior/display/setting, owner app, where it lives, deep link / console_open target, state read path, actions with parameters, parameter types, allowed values/ranges/defaults, needsAI flag, surfaces REST/MCP/CLI/voice). Extend the ui-api-parity and universal-voice-api-control declarations rather than replacing them. Write the JSON schema, a migration note for existing declarations, and the contract doc.
steps.why: Cross-port contract and schema design shared by console, Molly, axHub and the AmberX app

steps.text: Build the registry engine: collect entries from plugin manifests, ui-api-parity declarations and voice intents into one versioned offline index (JSON file plus in-memory query: list, get, search, by owner/type), with validation against the schema, change detection and an export/import for offline use. No AI anywhere in this path.
steps.why: Engine internals: the index every surface and the internal logic reads from

steps.text: Deterministic dispatcher with an AI-fallback gate: resolve a command, CLI call or voice phrase to a registry action and validated parameters using exact ids, aliases, synonyms and allowed values only. Fall back to Claude only when nothing matches and 'Make Claude available to the console' is on in Claude settings; otherwise return the closest registry matches and the gap. Reuse the universal-voice-api-control resolver.
steps.why: Engine internals that change how every app routes actions (no-AI-first rule)

steps.text: Console REST API for the registry and control: GET /api/registry (list/search/filter), GET /api/registry/:id, GET /api/registry/export, GET /api/control/:id/state, POST /api/control/:id/:action with parameter validation from the registry, POST /api/control/resolve (deterministic first, gated AI fallback). Auth and audit like the existing console API.

MCP tools on the same dispatcher: registry_list, registry_get, registry_search, control_state, control_invoke, control_resolve; map token and planner items to control@1 and keep console_show / console_open targets in sync with registry deep links.

CLI `axf ctl`: list, get, search, state, set, do, open, resolve, export; reads the offline index when the console is unreachable; argument validation and shell completion generated from the registry's parameters and allowed values.

Register the console itself: every page, plugin, tool, display option and setting with every parameter and allowed value, each with its deep link, state read and actions; fill gaps found against the ui-api-parity declarations.
Register Molly: pages, behaviors, settings and actions with parameters and allowed values, wired to the dispatcher and the four surfaces.
Register axHub: projects, connections, sync, profiles and settings, with deep links, state and actions; expose the provider bridge used by the next three steps.

Hostinger through axHub: domains, DNS records, VPS power/state, backups and plan info as registry entries with parameters and allowed values, called through the axHub connection (no direct secrets in the console).
Coolify through axHub: projects, applications, services, deployments, env vars, logs and restart/redeploy actions as registry entries with parameters and allowed values.
VPS through axHub: systemd services, processes, disk/memory state, logs, reboot and allow-listed maintenance commands as registry entries; destructive actions flagged and confirmation-gated.

AmberX app: register screens, settings and actions with Android deep links/intents, state read over the existing app channel, and voice phrases routed through the deterministic dispatcher with the gated AI fallback.
Moshi (third-party SSH app): find which deep links/intents it accepts, register only those (open host/session), mark everything else as an uncontrollable gap with the reason in the registry and docs.

Console Registry page: browse, search and filter all entries, see each entry's surfaces and gaps, run actions, and show whether the AI fallback is on. API part in the same step: deep link console_open target 'registry' (with id/query params), its state readable, its actions and filters callable via REST, MCP, CLI and voice, and the page registered in the registry itself.

Parity and coverage checker: fail when any UI page, setting or action lacks a registry entry or is missing any of REST/MCP/CLI/voice, or when a parameter has no allowed values; produce a gap report; add it to CI.

Tests (schema validation, index build, dispatcher no-AI paths and AI gate on/off, REST/MCP/CLI parity, provider mocks for Hostinger/Coolify/VPS, coverage check), write the report with how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice, add the THREADS row and open the PR.
